reason: At base the object JIT fastpass assigns the value of a swallowed issue for an absent optional key, so parsed output contains a:'leaked' instead of omitting the key. The test's expectation that no key exists fails.

At head the codegen guards both the issue concat and the assignment on !issues.length || present, so an absent optional key with a swallowed issue produces no key, and a present failing key still reports failure.
At base the paragraph continuation lookahead only treats a spaces-only line as blank, so a tab-only line is swallowed as lazy continuation and the two paragraphs merge into one.
At head the regex was widened to [ \t]+\n, so a tab-only line counts as blank and the two paragraphs are emitted separately.
The test checks normal JSON response parsing on a successful 200 request, which is unrelated to the error-path stack decoration code changed by this PR; it passes at base.
The change only touches the catch-branch stack decoration; successful JSON response parsing is unaffected and still returns a parsed object.
Parsing a plain boolean flag like --verbose is unrelated to the negative-number exponent regex changed by this PR; it works at base.
The only change is the negative-number regex accepting uppercase E; ordinary boolean flag parsing is unaffected.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt goes straight to JsonPrimitive.getAsInt/Integer.parseInt, which accepts full-width Unicode digits and silently yields 123 instead of raising a parse error.
At head nextInt validates that a STRING token is all-ASCII and throws MalformedJsonException for full-width digits, matching the expected error.
At base parseSearchPath uses an alphanumeric-only regex, so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' and the SQL becomes set search_path to "test", "db".
At head the regex is a delimiter blocklist [^\s,"']+, so 'test-db' stays a single token and the SQL sets one schema.
Default transformation behaviour for an ImageView request is unrelated to the ByteBufferUtil array-pool leak fix; it works at base.
The change only adds try/finally recycling in ByteBufferUtil.fromStream; the default isTransformationAllowed behaviour is untouched.
At base allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics is a computed property recalculated from the current allowedSymbols, so a configured extra symbol is always honoured and no violation is reported.

At head the union is cached and only refreshed by a didSet observer, which does not fire when the value is written through the ConfigurationElement property wrapper during configuration application or during initialization, so the cached set can stay plain alphanumerics and the identifier is flagged.
The PR only adds a <cstdint> include for GCC 15, so behaviour is unchanged; node-canvas does not percent-decode non-base64 SVG data URIs, so the image load fails.

Arrow's shift adds a relativedelta to the wall-clock time, so 18:30 + 10 hours yields 2025-03-09T04:30-05:00, not the 05:30 absolute-elapsed result the test expects; the Afrikaans locale change does not affect this.
The PR only adds a <cstdint> include, so behaviour is identical to base; node-canvas does not percent-decode non-base64 SVG data URIs before parsing, so the image fails to load.

The cookie-header change is unrelated. Vapor's request content container throws Abort(.unprocessableEntity) when the request body is empty, so decoding an all-optional type from an empty form-urlencoded body yields a 422 rather than a nil-filled instance.
Same as base: the PR only changes Cookie header directive parsing, and the empty-body decode path still aborts with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
The PR is a spelling-only change. Afero's MemMapFs.Remove has no emptiness check, so removing a non-empty directory succeeds instead of returning a 'directory not empty' error.
Identical behaviour to base — the diff only fixes comment/variable spelling; MemMapFs.Remove still deletes a non-empty directory without error.

The PR only fixes a json_encode call in a test, so the comparator is unchanged; the renamed-index detection still hits an undefined array key when one removed index has two equally matching added indexes.

The diff only fixes a json_encode argument in a test file, so the Comparator's renamed-index detection is unchanged and still triggers an undefined array key warning when one removed index matches two added indexes.
Arrow's shift performs wall-clock relativedelta arithmetic, giving 2025-03-09T04:30-05:00 rather than the expected 05:30; the Afrikaans locale PR does not touch this.

SemaphoreBasedRateLimiter.refreshLimit computes limit minus availablePermits and calls Semaphore.release with a negative value when the limit is lowered, throwing and causing the scheduled refresh task to be cancelled; the circuit-breaker PR is unrelated.
The head change only wraps CircuitBreaker predicates in try/catch; the rate limiter's negative Semaphore.release on a lowered limit still kills the scheduled refresh task.

The prefer-template PR is unrelated to no-var. no-var refuses to autofix when a reference to the variable appears textually before the declaration (TDZ hazard), so the file is left unchanged and still prints undefined.

Here the reference lives inside a function declared after the var statement, so no-var's TDZ heuristic does not block the fix; the rewritten let declaration makes the indirectly invoked function hit the temporal dead zone and throw a ReferenceError instead of printing undefined.
The PR only changes logformatter_adapter, so resume behaviour is unchanged; SitemapSpider with JOBDIR is a known case where the resumed run closes without crawling the remaining sitemap URLs.
Same as base — the log-formatting fix cannot affect scheduler persistence, so the resumed SitemapSpider run still closes with zero pages crawled.

The sanitize/bidi change does not touch the printer; at --terminal-width 1 a double-width character with a highlighted background still underflows the padding width computation and panics with a capacity overflow.

The head diff only affects the --sanitize preprocessor; the background-filling theme at terminal width 1 with double-width characters still triggers the same width-underflow panic, so the exit status is non-zero.
The syslog regex PR is unrelated. In out_file only one symlink is refreshed per flush, so a single batch carrying two distinct chunk keys leaves one of the two symlinks missing.
A follow-up event carrying a single previously-seen key produces one chunk, and the symlink for that key is created/updated normally; the RFC5424 regex change is unrelated.
The ConcurrentBag change is unrelated. HikariConfig.generatePoolName() synchronizes on System.getProperties(), so pool construction does take a lock shared with system-property access.

Although pool-name generation synchronizes on the system properties object, plain System.getProperty calls do not hold that monitor, so no lock-order inversion occurs and both threads complete; the ConcurrentBag change is unrelated.
The SORT ACL keyspec fix cannot affect RDB persistence, and the scenario describes the known 32-bit background-save failure, so the log does not report a successful termination.
Same behaviour as base — the diff only touches sortGetKeys and an ACL test; the 32-bit background save still fails once the dataset grows.

The cwd/context PR is unrelated. CTRL-A parses the number into a 64-bit integer; a 47-digit value overflows, so Neovim either refuses the increment or mangles the digits rather than producing the exact incremented value.
Same overflow limitation applies to CTRL-X at head; the context.c globaldir fix does not change number increment/decrement handling.
The external-file-cache race fix is unrelated to expression binding; DuckDB's || with an untyped NULL does not preserve the list type as the test expects.
Behaviour is identical to base since the diff only touches the file cache; typeof([1] || NULL) still disagrees with typeof(list_concat([1], NULL)).
NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE is a documented, supported notification for Object/RefCounted in Godot and the instance is still valid when it fires; the ScrollBar touch-input change is unrelated.
Same as base — reading a member variable during NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE works and does not crash; the ScrollBar diff cannot affect RefCounted destruction.

The decision-tree categorical change is unrelated. f_regression's force_finite=True default converts the undefined statistic for a constant feature into F=0.0 and p=1.0, and the divisions are wrapped in np.errstate so no RuntimeWarning is emitted.

r_regression computes np.sqrt(row_norms - n*mean**2) outside any errstate guard; with a near-constant column catastrophic cancellation makes the argument slightly negative, raising a RuntimeWarning about invalid value in sqrt.
The UI swagger change cannot affect the agent's file sink; Vault Agent's file sink applies the configured octal mode when writing the token file, giving 640.
Same unrelated UI-only diff; a configured mode of 0600 is applied by the file sink, so the token file is owner-only.

This is the PR's own regression scenario: at base write_usage with empty args passes an empty string through wrap_text, which discards the prefix and emits only a blank line, so the first help line is not 'Usage: cli'.
At head write_usage short-circuits when args is empty, writing the prefix and program name with the trailing separator stripped, producing exactly 'Usage: cli'.

Returning a dict from a view is converted to a compact application/json response by Flask's JSON provider; the IPv6 partition fix touches only app.run host parsing and the test client's cookie helper.
The head change does not touch response conversion, so a dict return is still serialized as compact JSON with an application/json content type.
Basic required-field validation is untouched by the DEPRECATED_ALIASES_IDS lookup change; a missing required field still raises a validation error naming it.
The head change only affects schema generation for unhashable generic aliases; required/missing field reporting is unchanged.
logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same value (30), so the default effective level and echo behaviour are identical; the test passes at base.
Purely a constant rename with identical semantics, so the echo-off/echo-on logging behaviour is unchanged.
At base, once attribute methods are generated, method_missing falls straight through to super for the aliased computed attribute, so the per-read overhead stays within the ~20x budget.

At head every method_missing call does self.class.public_instance_method(name) inside a begin/rescue NameError; raising and rescuing that exception 50,000 times for a non-column alias makes the access ratio far exceed 20x.
At base every dispatch pushes a fresh WrappedListener onto the callStack and getCalledListeners iterates it, so dispatching twice with one listener yields two entries.

At head called listeners are recorded in a deduplicated aggregate (each original listener stored only once per event) and the callStack is emptied, so getCalledListeners returns one entry instead of two.
The generated script tracks last_command as it walks the command line, so each subcommand's custom completion hook sees the right command; the shellcheck cleanups do not touch that logic.
The head diff only replaces word-splitting COMPREPLY assignments with read loops and adds an || return; custom completion hook dispatch based on last_command is unchanged.
qs's arrayLimit applies only to explicit numeric bracket indices; repeated plain keys are always combined into an array, so 25 repetitions of ids yield a 25-element array in qs 6.13.0.
qs 6.14.0 does not change how repeated plain keys are combined, so the parsed value is still an ordered 25-element array.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only a url argument, so calling it with just the URL returns the proxy dict without error.
The head signature is get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) with no default value, so calling it with only the URL raises TypeError for the missing argument.
At base parse_unit_value bails out immediately unless the first byte is a digit (or a minus followed by a digit), so '.foons' is never treated as a unit value and parses as a bare string.
At head a leading '.' enters unit parsing; '.foons' matches the 'ns' unit suffix and the remaining '.foo' fails to parse as a number, producing a parse error instead of the string.
At base a default temp-stream sink is always attached, so a HEAD request with an Accept-Encoding header completes and yields a response.
At head no sink is attached for HEAD requests, leaving EasyHandle::$sink unset; the response-finishing path then operates on a missing sink and raises a fatal error.
At base maps are left as values and simply inspected when formatting the diff, so an improper list inside a map renders fine and only the normal match error is reported.
At head escape/1 converts maps to AST via Map.to_list and build_map_or_struct; a value containing an improper list ([1 | 2]) is not valid AST for the formatter, so formatting the failure crashes.

This is the scenario the PR fixes: at base css_props tears down by removing the element and the dynamic-component codegen mismatches the css_props anchor, so after the toggle the custom property is lost/errors.
At head the teardown element removal is gone and dynamic components go through the same $.component/css_props ordering as SvelteComponent, so the color stays red across the toggle.

At base the plugin only checks code.includes('new URL') and includes('import.meta.url'), and the matching regex uses \s so it spans newlines; the multi-line reference is transformed and the asset emitted.

At head the transform is gated by the hook filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/, whose dot does not match newlines, so a multi-line new URL(...) never reaches the handler and the asset is not emitted.
At base no environment entry carries the item text, so a NUL-containing item does not affect launching the preview child process and the preview runs normally.
At head FZF_CURRENT_ITEM is built from the raw item text; with a NUL field delimiter the item contains a NUL byte, and an environment value containing NUL makes the exec of the preview command fail.
At base the EDGE_TO_EDGE branch falls through to setSystemUiVisibility with only the LAYOUT flags, clearing the immersive-sticky HIDE_NAVIGATION/FULLSCREEN flags so the system bars reappear.

At head the EDGE_TO_EDGE branch calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows and returns early without updating mEnabledOverlays or calling setSystemUiVisibility, so the previously applied immersive-sticky hide flags remain and the bars stay hidden.
At base there is no MultipleCaseAssignment check at all, so a class pattern with a keyword whose name equals the bound name produces no diagnostic.

At head the new visitor records class-pattern keyword attribute names in the same set as bound names, so Class(num_classes=num_classes) inserts 'num_classes' twice and a false 'multiple assignments to name' syntax error is reported under preview.
At base the decoder indexes the destination slice without growing it, so decoding two blocks into a one-element value slice panics with an index out of range.
At head the slice is appended to when the index exceeds its length, so both blocks decode and the field ends up with two entries.
At base the mock only calls setTimezone when an explicit timezone is given, so the mocked instance keeps its America/Los_Angeles zone and Carbon::now() formats in LA rather than the UTC default.
At head the mocked instance is converted with setTimezone($timezone ?? date_default_timezone_get()), so reading now() without a timezone yields the UTC representation.
The base regex /^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/ requires exactly two leading slashes followed by a non-slash, so '///test.com', '/\t//test.com' and '/\\/test.com' are not classified as protocol-relative.
The head regex /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/ allows three or more slashes, interleaved whitespace and mixed slash types, so all three inputs are reported protocol-relative with no explicit protocol.
Hashing.md5() of "abc" is unaffected by the combineOrdered/combineUnordered internal accessor change, so the standard digest is produced.
getBytesInternal returns the same bytes as asBytes without the defensive copy, and MD5 hashing is untouched, so the digest is still 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72.
Generating a stub for a properly attributed GET method works at base; the diagnostics refactor does not affect generation.
The change only relocates DiagnosticDescriptor definitions into a new compiled file with identical codes and messages, so generation and the emitted GET request are unchanged.
A plain HTTP/1.1 GET with a Content-Length body does not exercise the unknown-frame branch or the h2 paths touched here; it works at base.
Removing trailing continue statements and a clippy allow does not alter control flow for a simple HTTP/1.1 request/response exchange.
At base to_iso8601/2 converts the non-ISO date to Calendar.ISO and then calls to_iso8601/1, dropping the requested :basic format, so it returns the extended '2001-01-01'.
At head the format is forwarded (to_iso8601(format)), so the basic form '20010101' is returned for the Holocene-calendar date.
At base setEndDate updates only Carbon's internal endDate; the native DatePeriod::$end property is never re-synchronised on PHP 8.2+, so ->end still reports 2024-09-30.
At head setEndDate calls syncNativePeriod(), which re-runs parent::__construct with the new end date, so both ->end and getEndDate() report 2025-06-15.
At base headline builds the request line without validating whitespace, so a path containing a newline is transmitted instead of raising HTTP::RequestError.
At head headline raises RequestError 'Invalid request URI' when the resolved request URI matches /\s/, so the newline-containing path is rejected before sending.
English ToWords for 1000000/2000000 is unaffected by the Albanian locale YAML change; the default locale still yields 'one million' and 'two million'.
Only sq.yml and Albanian test data changed, so English number-to-words output is unchanged.
Singleton resolution from a Koin module does not touch saveProperties; the same instance is returned twice at base.
The property-loading fix does not affect single{} scoping, so both resolutions still return the identical instance.
At base replaceElement appends the new key/value, swaps them into position and pops the old pair, giving [a:1, z:2, c:3]; the duplicate-key precondition already guards the second call.
The refactor is equivalent: _replaceNew performs the same append/swap/removeLast on the keys while the value is overwritten in place, yielding the same contents, order and duplicate-key precondition.
At base parseSizeInBytes explicitly clamps a negative parsed size to 0, so '-5MB' yields 0 bytes.
max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is exactly equivalent to the removed negative-clamp, so '-5MB' still yields 0.

At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec takes children[0] when wildChild is set, which is the static child in this mixed static+param node, so the nType switch hits the default and panics — producing a server error instead of a redirect/404.

At head static children are tried via indices first and the wildcard child is taken from the end of the array, so the mis-cased path resolves to /prefix/xxx and the unmatched path simply returns not found.
At base toBigInt returns the nil Int when Exp is 0 and Int64Value then dereferences it, so a valid Numeric with no Int panics with a nil pointer dereference.
At head toBigInt returns big.NewInt(0) when Int is nil, so Int64Value returns zero and matches Float64Value without panicking.
External Quit() shutdown of the program loop is unrelated to the renderer's tab-stop handling, so the run call returns cleanly at base.
The change only affects SetTabStops and an ANSI tab-stop sequence when hard tabs are enabled; program shutdown on Quit is unchanged.

At base run_until_cancelled always builds RunUntilCancelledFuture and polls the wrapped future (biased toward completion), so the inner future that panics when polled is executed and the test panics instead of returning None.
At head the token's cancelled state is checked first and None is returned without ever constructing/polling the inner future, so no panic occurs.
Case-insensitive matching is unrelated to the ignore crate's walker optimization, so the search reports all mixed-case matches at base.
The change only avoids loading ignore files for skipped/max-depth directories; case-insensitive matching behaviour is unchanged.
At base a skip_deserializing field with no container default is given Default::Default, so the field gets its type's default value.
The refactor collapses the nested if into container_default.is_none() && ..., which is logically identical, so the skipped field still defaults.
